0.title: Discern – Unity Game
0.description:
Move in a 3D first-person environment and patrol rooms for unpredictable changes. Anomalies will show up periodically, so keep your eye out. Use your tablet to select the affected room and identify the correct anomaly category from 8 different types. Accurate reports will trigger a remote neutralization sequence. If you're not observant enough, anomalies will take over the area and lead to dire consequences.

The game is in a very early stage of development. Tutorial needs a rework and more maps are to be made, including new mechanics and anomaly types. The current build is playable and can be downloaded from https://tigerxplso.itch.io/discern

1.title: Smart Chatka Puchatka
1.description:
The project is a physical smart house for your pet. It consists of a ESP32 microcontroller connected to a camera, movement sensor, water pump, liquid level sensor, heater (simulated), and temperature sensor. It connects to a VPS via a mosquitto MQTT broker. The user can control the house via a web application or a mobile app, which allows them to monitor the pet's activity, check the sensor data, control the temperature, and check historical data from sensors with plots. The temperature can be controlled via a temperature threshold setting and can be additionally adjusted to a schedule. The user can invite others to be able to access the house and monitor the pet's activity. The initial setup is done via a simple QR-code scan. Once the house is set up, the QR code is no longer valid, to prevent unauthorized access. 

The backend and frontend are written in Python using Django. There is an additional admin panel and SSH access to the VPS for company employees. Everything is containerized using Docker and docker-compose and secured using SSL/TLS. The project was made under the SCRUM methodology and using kamban boards to monitor the progress. Collaboration was done using GitHub and Discord. Every week there was a stand-up meeting showing our progress. Also every week we had a retrospective meeting to discuss what went well and what could be improved. Instead of doing SCRUM Poker, all of us assigned story points to each task, after which we calculated a weighted average of the points to estimate the effort required for each task. This method accellerated the development process during complicated student life, without sacrificing quality. 
A demo presentation can be found on Youtube at https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1Ao9_D6l9R0

2.title: MCPedia – Discord Bot
2.description:
This Discord bot integrates the Minecraft Wiki (https://minecraft.wiki/) into Discord. It allows users to search any information about Minecraft. It also includes a simple and quick way to preview crafting recipes, calculate the amount of stacks or storage required to store a certain amount of items, and get the UUID of a player. Because fall damage in Minecraft is calculated in a weird way, the bot also includes a command to calculate the fall damage for a given height or says what heights are required to take a certain amount of damage. The bot is written in Python using the py-cord library. Unfortunately, because of lack of free python hosts, it hosted on my laptop, so it cannot be accessible publicly. For now it is only available to my community on our Discord server. The bot is still in development, so more commands will be added in the future. 
The source code is available on GitHub at https://github.com/malpkakefirek/MCPedia/ 
At the beginning of development, my friend helped me with a small part of the bot, but everything else was done by me.

3.title: Game Hub – Discord Bot
3.description:
This bot is meant to implement many games into Discord chat, to give more fun activities to server members. For now, it only includes Farkle, a dice game where players roll 6 dice and try to score points based on the combinations they roll, but more games are planned when bot hosting is established. In farkle, you can either invite someone specific to play with you or send a public invite for anyone willing to play with you. Farkle has more features planned, such as automatic loss detection and bots you can play against. There is also a scoreboard, but it is not yet fully implemented. 
The bot is written in Python using the py-cord library. It is hosted on my laptop, so it cannot be accessible publicly. For now it is only available to my community on our Discord server. 
The source code is available on GitHub at https://github.com/malpkakefirek/GameHub

4.title: MechBot – Discord Bot
4.description:
This is a community-centered bot, that provides social features to Discord servers. It includes a leveling system, where users can gain experience points by chatting in the server. It also includes a currency system, where users can earn coins by chatting or inviting others and use them to buy items from the shop, such as custom roles. The bot is written in Python using the py-cord library. The bot is directed specifically to the needs of my community, so it is not available publicly. 
The source code is available on GitHub at https://github.com/malpkakefirek/MechBot

5.title: SmartVent
5.description: SmartVent is a device that automatically opens and closes your window depending on the temperature, noise level, the air quality index, and the time of day. It allows the user to set the time, temperature, noise, and air quality thresholds. The user can also disable each threshold completely if needed and can manually override the window to be open or closed, either for a specified period of time or indefinitely until manually changed. User can connect remotely to the device via a web application to change any settings and preview the status and values. I was responsible for the hardware design and connecting every component to the raspberry Pi, as well as the backend of the web application. Collaboration was done using GitHub and Discord. Because of the short deadline of the project, it required intense collaboration and communication. To speed things up, my friend and I took on additional responsibilities to ensure the project's success, while some project members were lacking in contributions. The repository is available at https://github.com/jd-kowal/IoT---SmartVent

6.title: Schematics Website
6.description: This is the first iteration of a website that allows users to upload and download Minecraft build/redstone schematics, resource packs, and mods. The website is written in PHP with a PostgreSQL database. Because the website was hosted on student hosting provided by the university, it is no longer available. I collaborated with my friend on the frontend, backend, and database design. Unfortunately one member of our team didn't put in as much effort and provided lackluster contributions, that had to be re-written anyways, due to their poor quality. The website was designed to integrate well with the Minecraft graphic design and to be very user-friendly for dedicated Minecraft players. In a later project, we redesigned the website and focused on schematics. The source code for this website is available on GitHub at https://github.com/malpkakefirek/ProjektWWW-Schematics. The coding was done on university's architecture, so commit history does not reflect the actual development process.

7.title: Sapper Website
7.description: A fully functioning Minesweeper game implemented in Svelte with a Python backend. The game includes a shop with custom skins, boosters, xp system, battle pass, and friend system. The game system is designed to be fully asynchronous, so multiple players can play at the same time without any issues and game data is stored in a PostgreSQL database, so there is no risk of losing progress. I was mainly responsible for the backend and database design, while my friend was responsible for the frontend (don't blame me for the bad UI design). Because of the short deadline of the project and no prior experience with Svelte, I had to help with the frontend as well. The website is hosted on free hosting, therefore the dataset is also separated from the API server, so the latency is a lot higher than expected and sometimes the website may not work as expected. The website is publically available at https://sapper-zeta.vercel.app/ with the backend source code available at https://github.com/Malpkakefirek/SapperApi and the frontend source code available at https://github.com/Malpkakefirek/Sapper

8.title: Temperature Visualizer
8.description: A very simple temperature map visualizer, including temperature interpolation. You can input room dimensions and temperature values at some points in the room, and the program will generate a 3D temperature map of the room. The program is written in Python using Matplotlib for plotting. The interpolation is done using the scipy library.

9.title: Bookmaker Database Design
9.description:
My friend and I were tasked with designing a comprehensive database for a fictional bookmaker company. We did everything from creating a plan for the database, to designing the database schema, implementing it in PostgreSQL, and finally creating a comprehensive test suite. The database includes tables for users, workers, bets, football clubs, and transactions. The project was completed as part of our university coursework. 
The design principles can be found at https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Hd51_P9zIsXCqKzrTgrl8YtWTb_ZuTnqI_tibgu1JO0/edit?usp=sharing, the schema at https://docs.google.com/document/d/11M8eWLpypBQkiR6I5RKRsXGbkkHynCH1tCTmbYM6FYM/edit?usp=sharing, and the test suite at https://docs.google.com/document/d/1SiOuQZNdhILpWVutV8NLC7cb32DXIGlvKE0JT2TcvGU/edit?usp=sharing. 
All the documents in links are only in Polish.

10.title: School IT Network Design
10.description: Me and two of my friends were tasked with designing a comprehensive network for a ficticious school. The project included researching the ideal devices needed in the network, based on speed, max amount of concurrent users, price, energy consumption, operating temperatures, and other factors. We also designed the network topology, including the proper cabling and calculating all the prices, including the price of electricity. The final plan costs 12-15.5k PLN + 2k PLN per year for electricity and Librus subscription. All the images are in Polish.

11.title: Air Quality Forecast AI
11.description:
The aim of this project was to train a network to predict a certain parameter based on time series analysis. Me and my friend used a dataset of air quality measurements from AGH's meteorological station. The dataset included measurements of PM10, Air Pressure, Temperature, Humidity, Rainfall Intensity, and Wind Speed. We implemented a Random Forest (RF) model and a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model. The RF model was implemented using the scikit-learn library, while the LSTM model was implemented using the TensorFlow library. We used the models to predict future PM10 values based on all of the parameters. We also implemented an ARIMA model and compared all of their performance was evaluated using metrics such as Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE). The results showed that ARIMA is not sufficient for this task, while RF and LSTM models performed decently. Unfortunately, the amount of data was not sufficient to train the models properly, so the results were not very accurate and the differences between RF and LSTM were insignificant. The lack of data was addressed later as part of my engineering thesis, where I implemented a more complex model and used a large dataset from Airly. 
The source code is available on Colab at https://colab.research.google.com/drive/1gyvL_WkEVrbUbt-jeGi_YNN3OO5TGmyE?usp=sharing

12.title: Schematics Website Redesign
12.description:
This is a redesign of the Schematics Website project. This project focused solely on the UI/UX side of things, so no functioning website was made. It involved creating a new design centered around user experience, requiring a lot of reasearch of existing products, design principles, and user testing and feedback. 
The first step was to research existing products and analyze their strengths and weaknesses. The wesbites we looked at were: minecraft-schematics.com, planetminecraft.com, mcbuild.org, abfielder.com, schemat.io, and schematicmc.com. We also looked at minecraft.wiki and minecraft.net for design inspiration. After analyzing the websites, we wrote down our strategy, including every important aspect of the new design. Then, we created a google form to gather user needs and their current experience with existing products. After analyzing the results from 16 respondents, we created a user persona. Combining it with our strategy goals, we created a new design for the website, making sure to adhere to WCAG AAA standards. The design was then tested by 7 different users, that normally use existing products, with one of them also responding to the initial survey. The final design was then presented to our professor and received positive feedback. 
The design was created using the mobile-first design principle. The prototype was created using Figma, where unfortunately the font and some other assets are not how they would be in the final product.

14.title: Minecraft Builds
14.description:
This is not strictly related to game development, but it is somewhat related to world building. This is a collection of many of my Minecraft builds, from various servers over the years. All of them were built in survival mode, with original designs, never taken from the internet. Some of them were designed in creative mode before being build in survival, while others were built in survival with only a vague idea of what I want to build. If anything on the image was not designed by myself, it will be marked as such. 
The builds marked as "S1" were an allegedly abandoned house, that actually spies on a nearby military base. Unfortunately there wasn't enough time in the season to finish the builds. 
In "S2" I collaborated with my friend to build a castle on an island, with a city, farmlands, and a winery. All the interiors and details visible in the images were built by me, while the exteriors were mostly build by my friend. The inner-city contains a weaponsmith (with a shop), tannery, honey shop, canals, port, and other miscelaneous shops and buildings. Unfortunately we didn't have enough time to furnish every single building in the city. To the north of the city, there is a farm with a windmill and a barn, as well as a nice forest park (I don't have screenshots of the park, but the farm screenshot is taken from there). A path to the east from the city leads to the castle and further east to a winery. The castle has a throne room, royal quarters, library, planning room, kitchen, staff quarters, military strategy planning room, armory, and a business meeting room along with a waiting room on the top tower. 
Some planning was required to make sure everything is connected and has a purpose. The final product looks like a real lived-in city. The details really bring life to the builds.

15.title: Network Connect 4
15.description: A simple terminal connect 4 game, that allows two players to play against each other over a network. It was made in C and uses sockets for communication between players. One player acts as a server host and the other connects to it. The game is played in the terminal and uses ASCII characters to display the game board. I made sure to beautify the display to be as legible as possible. Code is available on GitHub at https://github.com/malpkakefirek/Connect4

16.title: Custom Cipher
16.description:
This is a cipher created by me. It's based on Vigenere cipher, but with a twist. It also scrambles the alphabet based on the key, which means the key itself also changes based on the key itself. The length of the message also changes depending on the key. It adds as many characters as there are in the key in places of the index of the key characters. But it adds letters based on the scrambled alphabet, so you can't guess the key even if you knew which characters are being added. The biggest flaws with this cipher are statistical analysis and PEBKAC with short keys. 
The source code is available on GitHub at https://github.com/malpkakefirek/malpka-cipher
